the use of Monte Carlo techniques with a focus on achievable subsets, along with alpha-beta pruning and squeaky wheel optimization, can produce an approximately expert caliber computer program to play the imperfect information game of contract bridge.
the Monte Carlo technique can be applied to realistic card play problems, and that it is possible to solve these problems approximately to the extent that they are solvable.

the use of partition search, the application of Monte Carlo methods, and the use (in conjunction with alpha-beta pruning) of achievable sets are sufficient to enable a program to play a realistic game of bridge, and that the use of squeak wheel optimization enables the program to play at expert level.
